DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES: - ["IfStatement", "SwitchCase", "TryStatement", "CatchClause", "ForStatement", "ForOfStatement", "ForInStatement", "WhileStatement", "DoWhileStatement"] - Annotated with @story 004.0 and @req REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA - This implements the "fallback scanning comment detection" for inline/before-case comments → REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION - For other branch nodes: - Uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node) and maps to comment.value - Returns concatenated comment text for annotation parsing - getBranchAnnotationInfo(sourceCode, node): - Uses gatherBranchCommentText - missingStory := !/@story\b/.test(text) - missingReq := !/@req\b/.test(text) - Computes indent and insertPos from sourceCode and node.loc - Provides the basis for annotation presence detection → REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING - reportMissingStory / reportMissingReq: - If first missing @story, inserts `// @story .story.md` above the branch via fixer and increments a shared counter - If @req missing and a story is present, inserts `// @req ` above the branch - Otherwise reports without fixer - This implements smart, limited auto-fix behavior and clear messages per missing annotation → Core Functionality & User Experience AC - reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef): - Calls getBranchAnnotationInfo - Builds actions array for story and req, then forEach over actions, invoking reportMissingStory/reportMissingReq only when missing == true - traceability.notes:
The story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented.
There is a dedicated ESLint rule (src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts) plus helpers (src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts) that detect significant branches (if/switch/loops/try-catch) and check for @story and @req in leading comments. Missing annotations are reported with clear, specific messages and selective auto-fixes. The rule supports configurable branchTypes with robust validation and explicit error messages for invalid configuration.
Tests in tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts and tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts comprehensively exercise valid/invalid branches for all supported node types, configuration edge cases, auto-fix behavior, and comment association (including the special SwitchCase scanning). All these tests pass in the current test run.
Rule documentation (docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md) is present, references the story, explains behavior and configuration, and includes correct/incorrect examples and invalid config examples. The rule is integrated into the plugin’s recommended and strict configs as an error.
Taken together, the implementation meets all the acceptance criteria and the listed requirements for this story based on concrete code and test evidence.
